ability-return-damage-weakness.setup:

blessed-salt-0hp.other: You (99% sure): it's Knocked Out at 0 before Blessed Salt can heal, and the opponent scores.

carefree-steps-snipe.engine: Since the rules pin (Oct 2, main-8626a35, repair B): the coin flips for snipe attacks at a Meowth, Benched or Active, and heads prevents the damage (apply_attack_action.rs, queued_attack_damage_choice; test carefree_steps_flips_for_a_direct_damage_snipe). The same covers Absol's Leap Over and Team Rocket's Hypno's Entrap. An Ability's damage (Greninja's Water Shuriken) never flips it (test carefree_steps_never_flips_for_an_abilitys_damage). Before the pin (main-d363ba8): no coin for snipes.
carefree-steps-snipe.look: Right after you pick Meowth as the target: does a Carefree Steps coin flip appear? Heads: no damage, Meowth stays on 50. Tails: the hit lands (Linear Attack's 50 Knocks it out). The coin appearing at all is the thing to see; a heads with 0 damage is the clearest.
carefree-steps-snipe.other: Card text / rules: the coin flips. Linear Attack, Tongue Whip, Leap Over and Entrap are attacks, and Carefree Steps covers any damage from attacks. Damage that isn't from an attack (an Ability like Greninja's Water Shuriken, Poison, Rocky Helmet) never flips it. Already seen in play: the coin flips when an ordinary attack hits an Active Meowth (155635 and 160256, both tails). Not seen yet: a snipe.

• If Meowth stays on the AI's Bench through your turn: deck 06's Heatmor (Tongue Whip, [R]) or deck 02's Absol (Leap Over, [D]). Deck 14's Team Rocket's Hypno (Entrap, [PP]) pulls a Benched Meowth into the Active Spot and hits it for 50, which counts too.

carefree-steps-snipe.sofar: Captured Oct 2 (20261002_161001000 + 20261002_161342000, one computer test battle; Codex/Sol review, Astra checked). carefree-steps-snipe.title: Meowth's Carefree Steps against a snipe attack

You said on Oct 1: "I think it will trigger on an attack, but it definitely won't from greninja's ability". The rules switch already follows that reading; nothing waits on this recording. Today's official simulator gives snipe attacks a sure hit on Meowth (a bug), and after the switch it's a coin. Meowth [B2 124] is in two Limitless archetypes (Garchomp and Meowth, 20 lists; Togekiss and Meowth, 4), and four of your decks have snipe attacks that hit it: 08 (Gabite), 06 (Heatmor), 02 (Absol), 14 (Team Rocket's Hypno).

At setup put Eevee Active and Rattata on the Bench. On your first turn (turn 1 if you go first, turn 2 if second), tap Raticate ex in your hand.
A throwaway deck with a second pair (2 Swablu [B1 196] and 2 Mega Altaria ex [B1 102] on top of these six) makes it about 1 start in 7; then a Benched Swablu is the target to watch as well.

eevee-boosted-evolution-only-eevee.title: Eevee's Boosted Evolution: only Eevee evolves on turn 1
eevee-boosted-evolution-only-eevee.why: The meta Altaria list runs 2 Eevee [B1 184] next to 2 Swablu and Mega Altaria ex. If Boosted Evolution spread to the whole board, a Benched Swablu could become Mega Altaria ex on turn 1; that was the old simulator bug (rules/README). fossil-and-tool-type-lines.engine: Our card database stores a Fossil's type as "Fossil", not "Item". fossil-and-tool-type-lines.other: Plain reading: an Item lock stops exactly the cards whose kind is Item. The question is only what the card's kind line says.
fossil-and-tool-type-lines.setup: No game needed: just the card view of one Fossil and one Pokémon Tool from your collection.
fossil-and-tool-type-lines.sofar:

fossil-and-tool-type-lines.title: The type line on a Fossil card and on a Pokémon Tool (two pictures, no game)
fossil-and-tool-type-lines.why: Checks what the cards themselves say, the plain text your Oct 1 rule goes by. It only matters for decks that play Fossils or Tools against an Item lock, so it's low priority, but it takes a minute.
